clue.text: Killer's form of Old Testament drama

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means they are rearranged into a different shape

explanation.surface: A theatrical piece based on a Bible story turns out to be about murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' asks for an anagram of OT plus DRAMA, giving the bullfighter's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The matador is the bullfighter whose role is to kill the bull at the end of the fight.

clue.text: Motorway madness an illusion?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
rage can mean madness or fury

explanation.surface: Road rage on the motorway is just in the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, such as water seen in a desert, caused by refraction of light.

clue.text: Make a mistake over oil output in N Africa

parts.note: to trip is to slip up or make a mistake

indicators.note: output suggests the word oil is put out in a new form

explanation.surface: An error over oil production in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' links the two pieces; 'output' anagrams OIL into OLI, giving the Libyan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, on the North African coast.

clue.text: Sort of paper said to do the vanishing trick

indicators.note: to sort letters is to arrange them, so these words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A stage magician makes a sheet of paper vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' scrambles PAPER and SAID together; 'said' is fodder here, not a sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to cease to be visible, as a conjuror's assistant does.

clue.text: Refinement of unusual political clique

parts.note: something unusual is rare
a faction is a dissenting clique within a party

explanation.surface: A rare sophistication among a party's inner circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Rarefaction is the thinning of a gas, a process of making it less dense or refined.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarefaction means making something thinner or purer, reducing its density, a kind of refining.

clue.text: Pertinent note on composer, perhaps

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another comes straight after it

parts.note: Sir Edward German was an English composer of light opera
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A musical note added to a score is relevant to the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' warns that the composer is a particular one: Edward German, who wrote the comic opera Merrie England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something relevant and to the point in a discussion.

clue.text: Geyser's origin as a source of heat

indicators.note: a word's origin is where it starts, so its opening letter is wanted

explanation.surface: Where a geyser gets its heat.
explanation.walkthrough: A geyser is also a British gas-fired water heater, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is burned as a fuel for cooking and heating homes.

clue.text: One reaching higher position in flight

explanation.surface: Someone climbing up the ranks while on the run.
explanation.walkthrough: A riser is one who rises; it is also the vertical part of each step in a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who climbs socially is a riser, and the upright face of a stair step bears the same name.

clue.text: Preacher extremely late after an appointment

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes later in the answer

parts.note: a post is a job or appointment

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A minister turns up very late following his appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'late', LE, which go after A POST.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the disciples sent out by Christ to spread the gospel, preaching missionaries.

clue.text: Hasten training said in France to be held in river

indicators.note: held in means placed inside the word for the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England
PE is physical education, training
dit is French for said

explanation.surface: Hurry up the training, someone in France says, during the river trip.
explanation.walkthrough: PE and DIT go inside EXE, giving EX-PEDIT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite a task is to speed it up or hurry it along.

clue.text: Certain inside control provides secondary cover

indicators.note: one word placed inside another, here the word for certain going within the reins

parts.note: reins are what a rider uses to control a horse, so control can mean reins
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Being sure of one's grip on things lets an insurer lay off its risks.
explanation.walkthrough: Reinsurance is when an insurer passes part of a risk it holds to another insurer.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer who lays off risk with a second insurer takes out backup policies on what it already covers.

clue.text: Custom, perhaps, in a jazz dance? On the contrary

indicators.note: the letters sit within the words before it; the clue says the dance is in them, not the other way round

parts.note: the dance's letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Is a tradition kept up inside a jazz routine? Quite the reverse, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' with 'On the contrary' flips the surface: the custom is not in a jazz dance; a jazz dance is in 'Custom, perhaps', spanning cuSTOM Perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomp is a lively jazz dance with heavy stamping steps, popular in the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: Set to reach maturity out West

indicators.note: out says the letter for West is removed from the phrase meaning reach maturity

parts.note: to reach maturity is to grow up
W is the compass abbreviation for West

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to come of age out on the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W from GROW UP to leave the word for a set or collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of things is a collection of them taken together, a cluster or batch.

clue.text: Joined together to eat without trade disruption

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so the word for eating goes round the rest

parts.note: to feed is to eat, as animals do

indicators.note: disruption suggests the letters of the word next to it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Several parties united to eat, free of any industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption' gives DERAT from TRADE, and 'without' means outside: FEED goes round it, FE-DERAT-ED. The file's 'cat' is an OCR slip; the page prints 'eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: States that have federated have united into a single federation, keeping some local powers.

clue.text: Fellow holding up fishermen's catches on board

indicators.note: in a down clue the fellow sits below the catches and so holds them up

parts.note: a draught is a haul of fish in a net, as in the Bible's miraculous draught of fishes
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man carries the day's catch onto a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A draughtsman is also a playing piece in draughts (checkers), so 'on board' points to a game board, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtsman is one of the round counters moved across the board in the game of checkers.

clue.text: Frustration experienced eventually by the Sleeping Beauty

definitions.text: experienced eventually by the Sleeping Beauty

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale princess finally grows fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word literally: dis-enchantment, the breaking of the spell that kept the princess asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Frustration is disappointment and disillusion; the Sleeping Beauty eventually had her magic spell lifted when the prince kissed her.

clue.text: So cute, in a strange way, though stubborn

indicators.note: putting letters in a strange way means jumbling them

explanation.surface: Being sweet in an odd manner, yet obstinate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange way' rearranges SO CUTE and IN A; 'though' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenacious person holds firmly to a course, refusing to give up.

clue.text: Last word about king in a novel from Transcaucasia

indicators.note: about places the word for king inside the prayer's closing word

parts.note: amen is the last word of a prayer
R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the two short words before it take a new order

explanation.surface: The closing line about a monarch in a book set in the Caucasus.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside AMEN, giving ARMEN; 'novel' rearranges IN A into IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia lies south of the Caucasus mountains, in the region called Transcaucasia.

clue.text: Attendant of low order may have us all taped

definitions.text: Attendant of low order may have us all taped

parts.words: Attendant of low order may have us all taped
parts.note: a minor heavenly being who keeps a written account of every person's good and bad deeds, imagined as running a tape

explanation.surface: A lowly servant has everyone figured out.
explanation.walkthrough: Angels are the lowest of the nine orders of heavenly beings; this one notes down all our deeds, and 'taped' is turned into a modern recording.
explanation.definitionFit: In tradition a minor heavenly being keeps a register of each person's good and bad actions for Judgment Day.

clue.text: Large sum needed to support Tom's favourite in bed!

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece stands underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a mint is a large sum of money

explanation.surface: A fortune is needed to keep a pet happy in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: MINT goes under CAT. Catmint, or catnip, is a garden plant cats love, so 'bed' is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint grows in garden borders and drives felines wild, so it is their preferred plant there.

clue.text: Formerly a universal vessel made of cast-offs?

parts.note: ex means former, once
U is the film certificate for universal viewing
a vial is a small glass vessel

explanation.surface: An old jar once used by all, now put together from discarded bits.
explanation.walkthrough: Exuviae are the cast-off skins or shells of animals such as snakes and insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuvial describes the shed skins or shells that creatures moult and leave behind.

clue.text: Stopped being serious demeanour, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: staid describes someone of sober, serious bearing

explanation.surface: Someone stopped being so sober-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; STAID and STAYED sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have remained in place, halted rather than moving on.

clue.text: Cafe where poor men sit and eat?

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A humble eatery where impoverished men can sit down to a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' scrambles MEN SIT and EAT together into the French word for a small cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French cafe or bar, familiar to British soldiers in the First World War.

clue.text: The Warden's reading matter

parts.note: not a novel but the device whose display a traffic warden checks when deciding on a parking ticket

explanation.surface: A book the warden of a college might read.
explanation.walkthrough: The Warden is a Trollope novel; here it is a traffic warden, who reads the display on a parking device. A British traffic warden enforces parking rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic wardens check the timer at a parking bay to see whether the paid time has run out.

clue.text: Unwisely invite flattering attention

explanation.surface: Asking for compliments in a foolish way.
explanation.walkthrough: One courts disaster by inviting it unwisely; a suitor pays court to someone with flattering attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To court trouble is to risk bringing it on, and paying court means wooing someone with compliments.

clue.text: 26, an eponymous Dostoievskian hero

explanation.surface: A reference to another clue, naming a title character from Russian fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' points to the answer at 26 across, NATURAL, in its old sense of a simpleton. Prince Myshkin is the hero of Dostoevsky's novel named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural once meant a person born simple-minded, and Dostoevsky's novel about Prince Myshkin bears this title.

clue.text: No member thus returned? Pity about such self-importance

indicators.note: about means the letters of the word pity go round the other pieces

parts.note: no can be nought, the letter O
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: returned says the word for thus is read backwards

parts.note: thus means so

explanation.surface: An MP fails to be re-elected; what a shame, given such a puffed-up character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SO into OS; O, MP and OS go inside PITY, with 'about' as the container signal, giving P-OMPOS-ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomposity is an inflated sense of one's own importance shown in manner and speech.

clue.text: Chum of a student from Pittsburgh, for instance

parts.note: Pittsburgh is a city in Pennsylvania, abbreviated PA
L is the learner driver's plate, a student

explanation.surface: A friend of an American student.
explanation.walkthrough: Pittsburgh stands for its state, Pennsylvania, whose postal code is PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is a friend or mate.

clue.text: This hand makes twenty-one on the staff

explanation.surface: A card hand scores the maximum, and someone is employed.
explanation.walkthrough: In blackjack, an ace and a ten-card dealt first is a natural; on a musical staff a natural sign cancels a sharp or flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackjack term for an unbeaten opening pair, and a musical sign written on the stave cancelling a sharp or flat.

clue.text: Way student in want settled comfortably

indicators.note: in places the way and student letters inside the word for want

parts.note: to want something is to need it
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
L is the learner driver's plate, a student

explanation.surface: A student short of money finds a cosy place to live anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: ST and L go inside NEED, giving NE-STL-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle is to settle snugly into a comfortable position, like a bird in its nest.
